narrative:

The most influential factor in this prediction was your performance in your third year, where you ranked in the lowest decile compared to your peers. This suggests that your academic performance during this critical period was considerably below average, as students who were accepted typically ranked much higher. Additionally, your first-year ranking also contributed negatively, being below the average decile for accepted students. 

Your family income level, categorized as lower-middle, was another factor that influenced the prediction. While this alone does not determine success, it can correlate with access to resources that support academic achievement. In contrast, a significant portion of accepted students come from upper-middle and middle-income backgrounds, which may provide more opportunities for academic support.

Together, these factors led to the conclusion that your likelihood of passing the bar exam was lower than desired. To improve your chances for future applications, consider focusing on enhancing your academic performance, particularly in your final year, and exploring resources that can help you strengthen your study habits and exam preparation. Engaging in additional support systems, such as tutoring or study groups, may also be beneficial.
